```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

teal <- "#0D9488"
ink  <- "#052E2B"

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          axis.text  = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"))
)

efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")
d <- zap_labels(efcu) |>
  mutate(awareness = factor(q13_r, levels = 1:3,
                            labels = c("Unaware", "Aware, not used", "Aware and used")))

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
```

## About this report

This report tests the first two hypotheses for Case 31 using the cleaned data (**n = 128 members**).

- **H1:** Members' **awareness of regular share accounts** (Q13r) will influence their opinion on **how well the CU's financial services meet members' needs** (Q33).
- **H2:** Members will **not differ** in their opinion of **the CU's loan rates** (Q8r) and their agreement that **CU loan rates are lower than competitors'** (Q30).

The tests follow the data analysis table: a **one-way ANOVA** for H1 and a **paired-samples t-test** for H2. Each section shows the **descriptive statistics first**, then the test, then the **insight**. Statistics stay in parentheses and point to numbered tables and figures.

## H1: Awareness of regular share accounts → services meet needs

### H1: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h1-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Agreement that the CU's services meet members' needs (Q33), by awareness of regular share accounts (Q13r)"
h1_desc <- d |>
  group_by(Awareness = awareness) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `% agree (4–5)` = 100 * mean(q33 >= 4),
            `% disagree (1–2)` = 100 * mean(q33 <= 2),
            Mean = mean(q33), SD = sd(q33), Median = median(q33))
h1_desc |> kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h1
#| fig-cap: "Mean agreement that services meet members' needs, with 95% confidence intervals, by awareness of regular share accounts"
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 9
d |>
  group_by(awareness) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(q33), se = sd(q33) / sqrt(n),
            lo = mean - qt(.975, n - 1) * se, hi = mean + qt(.975, n - 1) * se) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, fct_rev(awareness))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "#9a9a9a") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0.18, color = ink, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 5, color = teal) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f  (n = %d)", mean, n)), vjust = -1.3,
            color = ink, fontface = "bold", size = 4.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(2.5, 4.3), breaks = seq(2.5, 4.5, 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Mean agreement: services meet my needs (1–5)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### H1: Assumption check (equal variances)

```{r}
#| label: h1-bartlett
h1_bart <- bartlett.test(q33 ~ awareness, data = d)
h1_bart
```

The three groups have **similar spread** (Bartlett's K²(2) = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_bart$statistic)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h1_bart$p.value)`), so the regular ANOVA is appropriate.

### H1: One-way ANOVA

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h1-anova
#| tbl-cap: "One-way ANOVA: Q33 by awareness of regular share accounts"
h1_aov <- aov(q33 ~ awareness, data = d)
h1_tab <- summary(h1_aov)[[1]]
eta2   <- h1_tab[["Sum Sq"]][1] / sum(h1_tab[["Sum Sq"]])
tibble(Source = c("Awareness (Q13r)", "Residuals"),
       df = h1_tab$Df, `Sum Sq` = h1_tab$`Sum Sq`, `Mean Sq` = h1_tab$`Mean Sq`,
       F = h1_tab$`F value`, p = c(fmt_p(h1_tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]), "")) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: h1-robust
h1_welch <- oneway.test(q33 ~ awareness, data = d)
h1_kw    <- kruskal.test(q33 ~ awareness, data = d)
```

### H1: Post-hoc test (Tukey HSD)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h1-tukey
#| tbl-cap: "Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons of mean Q33"
TukeyHSD(h1_aov)$awareness |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("Comparison") |>
  transmute(Comparison, `Mean difference` = diff, `95% CI lower` = lwr,
            `95% CI upper` = upr, `Adjusted p` = fmt_p(`p adj`)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

### H1: Insight

::: {.takeaway}
**H1 is SUPPORTED, but in a surprising direction: the members who actually USE regular share accounts are the LEAST satisfied that EFCU meets their needs.**
:::

- **Unaware and aware-but-not-used members look the same.** About **63% agree** that services meet their needs, with means of **3.63 and 3.72** (@tbl-h1-desc).
- **Members who have used regular share accounts stand apart.** Only **31% agree** and their mean drops to **3.08**, barely above neutral (@fig-h1).
- **The differences are real, not chance** (*F*(2, 125) = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_tab$"F value"[1])`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h1_tab$"Pr(>F)"[1])`, η² = `r sprintf("%.2f", eta2)`; @tbl-h1-anova). The **"used" group is lower than both other groups** (Tukey *p* = .017 and .011), while the other two don't differ (*p* = .782; @tbl-h1-tukey).
- **The result holds up** with the Welch ANOVA (*p* = `r fmt_p(h1_welch$p.value)`) and the non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test (*p* = `r fmt_p(h1_kw$p.value)`), which matters because the "used" group is **small (n = 13)**.
- **So what:** the people with the **most hands-on experience** of EFCU's core account are the **least convinced** it meets their needs. Experience seems to expose gaps that non-users never see. EFCU should **talk to its active account users** to find out what's missing, whether that's rates, features or convenience. Because the group is small, this is a **strong signal to investigate**, not a final verdict.

## H2: Opinion of CU loan rates vs. "CU rates are lower than competitors"

### H2: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: h2-data
h2 <- d |> select(Q8_r, q30, q8) |> drop_na()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h2-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Loan rate opinions among members who answered both questions"
tibble(
  Item = c("Q8r: CU loan rates (1 = very low, 5 = very high)",
           "Q30: CU loan rates lower than others (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)"),
  n = nrow(h2),
  `% at midpoint (3)` = c(100 * mean(h2$Q8_r == 3), 100 * mean(h2$q30 == 3)),
  `% 4–5` = c(100 * mean(h2$Q8_r >= 4), 100 * mean(h2$q30 >= 4)),
  `% 1–2` = c(100 * mean(h2$Q8_r <= 2), 100 * mean(h2$q30 <= 2)),
  Mean = c(mean(h2$Q8_r), mean(h2$q30)),
  SD = c(sd(h2$Q8_r), sd(h2$q30))
) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-h2
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of answers to Q8r and Q30 (same members, n = 107)"
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-width: 10
h2 |>
  select(`Q8r: CU loan rates are high` = Q8_r, `Q30: CU rates lower than others` = q30) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") |>
  count(item, value) |>
  group_by(item) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(value), pct)) +
  geom_col(fill = teal, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct)), vjust = -0.4, color = ink,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(item, levels = c("Q8r: CU loan rates are high", "Q30: CU rates lower than others"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 65), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Response (1–5)", y = "% of members") +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold", size = 14))
```

### H2: Paired-samples t-test

```{r}
#| label: h2-ttest
h2_t <- t.test(h2$Q8_r, h2$q30, paired = TRUE)
h2_t
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-h2-t
#| tbl-cap: "Paired-samples t-test: Q8r vs. Q30"
tibble(Comparison = "Q8r − Q30", n = nrow(h2),
       `Mean difference` = unname(h2_t$estimate),
       `95% CI lower` = h2_t$conf.int[1], `95% CI upper` = h2_t$conf.int[2],
       t = unname(h2_t$statistic), df = unname(h2_t$parameter),
       p = fmt_p(h2_t$p.value)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

### H2: Direction check (correlation and aligned comparison)

The two items **run in opposite directions**. A high Q8r means a member thinks EFCU's rates are **high** (bad for the member), while a high Q30 means they agree EFCU's rates are **lower** than competitors' (good for the member). The correlation confirms it:

```{r}
#| label: h2-direction
h2_r       <- cor.test(h2$Q8_r, h2$q30)
h2_aligned <- t.test(h2$q8, h2$q30, paired = TRUE)
h2_r
h2_aligned
```

### H2: Insight

::: {.takeaway}
**H2 is SUPPORTED as stated: members see EFCU's loan rates as "average," and they're no more convinced the rates beat competitors'.**
:::

- **Both answers cluster in the middle.** **55% call EFCU's loan rates "average"** on Q8r, and **41% are uncertain** whether they beat other lenders on Q30 (@tbl-h2-desc, @fig-h2).
- **The two means are practically identical**: **3.14 vs. 3.06**, with no significant difference (*t*(106) = `r sprintf("%.2f", h2_t$statistic)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h2_t$p.value)`; @tbl-h2-t). So the hypothesis of no difference holds.
- **A caution on reading this:** the two items point in **opposite directions**, and members answer them consistently. Those who think rates are high tend to disagree that rates beat competitors (*r* = `r sprintf("%.2f", h2_r$estimate)`, *p* < .001). When Q8 is put on the same direction as Q30 (original Q8, where 5 = very low), members are **slightly more positive about rates compared with competitors** than about rates in absolute terms, though the gap is **small** (2.86 vs. 3.06; *t*(106) = `r sprintf("%.2f", h2_aligned$statistic)`, *p* = `r fmt_p(h2_aligned$p.value)`).
- **So what:** **price is not a selling point for EFCU loans**. Members see the rates as neither cheap nor expensive, and they aren't sure EFCU beats the competition. That matches R2, which pointed to **loan rates as the most likely reason members borrow elsewhere**. **Sharper, clearly communicated loan pricing** is the lever.

## Summary

| Hypothesis | Test | Result | Insight |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **H1** | One-way ANOVA + Tukey | **Supported** (*F*(2, 125) = 4.63, *p* = .012) | **Members who use regular share accounts are the LEAST satisfied** that EFCU meets their needs (31% agree vs. ~63%) |
| **H2** | Paired-samples t-test | **Supported: no difference** (*t*(106) = 0.60, *p* = .549) | Members see loan rates as **average** and **aren't sure they beat competitors**, so **price isn't a selling point** |
